mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes SLC 180 or 200 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M274 engine for the SLC 180 costs £3,200-£4,400 supply-only; a rebuilt M274 engine for the SLC 200 costs £3,400-£5,200 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,200 depending on complexity - modern turbocharged work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes SLC 180 or 200?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the M274 engine. The timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack and guide wear. If ignored, it can lead to catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: What causes oil consumption in a Mercedes SLC 180 or 200?

acceptedAnswer.text: One of the most prevalent issues with the M274 engine is excessive oil consumption. A class action lawsuit has alleged a piston defect causing premature failure in M274 engines. Worn piston rings can also allow oil to bypass into the combustion chambers.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes SLC 180 or 200 engine (M274) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M274 engine is a modern, efficient turbocharged four-cylinder, but it has known issues. Timing chain tensioner wear, thermostat failure, and piston ring wear are the most common problems. With these addressed, the engine is capable of 100,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes SLC 180 and 200 engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M274 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. Timing chain tensioner issues typically appear between 45,000-80,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes SLC 180 or 200?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the SLC is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M274 costs £3,200-£5,200 - far less than replacing a £12,000-£25,000 vehicle. SLC values remain strong for well-maintained examples, making engine replacement a worthwhile investment.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz SLC 180/200 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The SLC 180 and SLC 200 launched in 2016 as the rebadged successors to the SLK, powered by the modern M274 turbocharged four-cylinder engine family. The SLC 180 featured a 1.6-litre version producing 156hp, while the SLC 200 received a 2.0-litre unit delivering 184hp. Both engines featured direct injection and turbocharging, replacing the earlier M271 supercharged and turbocharged engines. Production continued until 2020 when the SLC was discontinued, making these models the final chapter of Mercedes' compact roadster lineage.

milestones.description: 2020 - Both engines continue with 9G-TRONIC automatic transmission from 2016
End of SLC production; R172 platform retired

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz SLC 180 and 200 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from M274 timing chain tensioner wear to thermostat failure and piston ring wear.

problems.h4: M274 Piston Ring Wear & Oil Consumption - The Modern Engine's Lubrication Challenge
problems.rootCause: One of the most prevalent issues with the M274 engine is excessive oil consumption. A class action lawsuit has alleged that certain M274 engines suffer from a defect causing the pistons to fail prematurely. This piston defect can occur without warning and cause sudden and unexpected engine failure. Oil consumption can also be caused by worn piston rings allowing oil to bypass into the combustion chambers.
